name: Haven Station
desc: A neutral trade hub where every faction drinks in the same bar and pretends not to notice.

gm.feel: Frying synth-fat, ozone and old beer, under lighting that was meant to be temporary forty years ago. Every wall has a fee schedule bolted to it, and it's usually been amended by hand. Hegemony officers, Syndicate fixers and refugee mothers queue at the same noodle hatch, not looking at one another with tremendous skill.

districts.name: The Neutral Ground
districts.desc: Jun Sable's bar, where weapons go in a locked rack by the door and any feud has to wait outside. Sable has broken up exactly one fight here, and the stain is kept as a warning.

districts.name: The Manifest Docks
districts.desc: Forty berths under Dockmaster Mott Jessup, who knows what every ship is really carrying. Docking is charged by the hour, and the hour is whatever he says it is.

districts.name: The Consulate Row
districts.desc: A polished corridor of offices flying the flags of governments that may no longer exist. Legate Corvane's has the only real carpet on the station.

districts.name: Tharel's Warm Room
districts.desc: A former boiler compartment, kept hot for the old Thessan archivist and his crates of paper. It's the only place on Haven where nobody is selling anything.

districts.name: The Hook
districts.desc: Refugee overflow in a disused cargo spine. People hang their belongings from the old cargo hooks, and sell them one at a time.

complications: Mott Jessup has quietly raised your docking fee, and the fine print says your ship can't leave until it's paid.
Someone has broken the truce in the Neutral Ground, and Sable wants to know who's going to pay for the glass.
Legate Corvane has just made a very public offer in front of a crowd of your own refugees, with a smile.
A station inspector has found a discrepancy on your manifest, and it's a small one, and he'd love to discuss it.
The Hook's air scrubbers fail again, and five hundred angry people decide it's the captain of the fleet's problem.
Sister Yara Solune is preaching at the far end of the dock, and a frightened crowd is deciding what to do about her.
secrets: Mother Quill's Syndicate holds the mortgage on Haven's docks through three shell companies, and that's the real reason the station can afford to stay neutral.
A bulkhead behind Sable's bar hides a dead-drop relay left from Concord Intelligence, and it's still receiving something.

Every month, unmarked Hegemony ships refuel at a back dock, going out past the border full and coming back empty. Mott Jessup took the money without asking until he looked through a hatch one night. He's kept a private copy of every manifest since, and he can't think who it'd be safe to tell.

encounters: Jun Sable slides you a drink you didn't order and a bill for it that's much too high. The price, they explain without looking up, includes the name of the person who's been asking about your ship.

A Hegemony junior attache and a Syndicate fixer are arguing over a card game at the next table in the Neutral Ground. Each of them separately catches your eye and quietly asks you to say the other one cheated.

Dockmaster Mott Jessup offers to lose an entry from your manifest, and he's open about the several currencies he accepts: credits, a favor, or a look at someone else's manifest. He's already holding a look at yours.

Sister Yara Solune is sitting on a crate in the Hook, holding the hand of a dying refugee and glowing softly, and the old man has stopped being afraid. His daughter is thanking her. His son has gone to find a length of pipe.

Archivist Tharel is trying to move his crates to a warmer deck, and he's too frail and too proud to ask. He calls you young one, and he remarks that one of the crates is not, strictly speaking, the property of the person he took it from.

A boy of about nine is selling a working Concord service medal in the Hook, with the name carefully filed off. He says it's his mother's. A ragged lieutenant two stalls down hasn't stopped staring at him.

Legate Corvane catches up with you in the corridor, delighted, as though you'd arranged to meet. He has a contract with your fleet's name already typed in, and he only wants you to read one page of it, as a friend.

A woman in the noodle queue recognizes you, and she doesn't shout. She takes a picture of her husband out of her coat and asks whether you were the one who gave the order to leave the Tannhal Orbitals. You weren't, but she won't believe you easily.

A docker on Mott's crew finds you and says, very low, that a crate marked as grain for your fleet weighs about a third of what it should. He wants fifty credits to say which one, and he wants to be gone before you open it.

Two refugees are auctioning their berth on a departing freighter to a crowd in the Hook. One of the bidders is a hard-faced man who keeps bidding on behalf of someone else, and he's paying far above what it's worth.

A young woman in a fleet coat asks you, quite politely, to confirm her father's death, because the Hegemony office won't accept her transit claim without it. You don't know the name. Saying yes would get her out.

A bounty hunter buys you a drink under the truce rules. She wants to tell you in good faith that she's working a warrant on someone on your crew, and that she'll start once you're both past the weapon rack.

A very drunk Thessan consul from one of the flags on Consulate Row insists on presenting you with a formal diplomatic recognition of your fleet. It's probably worthless. It's also legally binding, and he has a stamp.

The station's chief air technician waits outside the Neutral Ground, twisting her cap. The Hook's scrubbers have about four days left, Mott won't pay for filters, and she wants you to know before everyone else does.

A cheerful stranger offers you an unbelievable price on fuel from a tanker he says is docked at berth nineteen. Berth nineteen is real, and so is the tanker. The trouble starts when you ask to see who's aboard it.
rumors: Word at the Neutral Ground is that Sable has never once forgotten a tab. They say it's still open on a Concord admiral who's been dead six months, and that the estate will be hearing from them.
Don't take the first fee Mott quotes you. Don't take the second, either. The third one's real, and by then he's found out what you're carrying.

A signals tech at the Neutral Ground swears the Beacon's got plain Navy format sitting on top of something much older. Safe harbor, all Concord vessels come home. So who's home, then? He's asking for a friend, and the friend is me.
That old lizard in the boiler room has been reading the Beacon's signal for weeks. Ask him what he thinks, and watch how long he takes to change the subject.
The Quiet girl at the end of dock six, the one who glows, she sat with my mother at the end. I'd give anything to say I hated her for it.
Fuel's going up again by the end of the week. I don't know who's behind it, but it's somebody who knows exactly how many ships you've got.
They'll tell you Haven's neutral because everyone needs it. It's neutral because somebody owns the paper on it, and that somebody likes it this way.
Legate Corvane's offer is real, I've seen it. A berth, three meals and a place in the ranks. Mind you, I've never met anyone who wrote back to say how it's going.
A Hegemony transport took on four hundred refugees here last month. Only three hundred and sixty signed the manifest at the other end, and no one's said a word about it.

There's a stain on Sable's floor that they won't clean. Some say it was a Syndicate boss. Others say an Inquisitor. The Ground's regulars say it was a health inspector, and that's why there hasn't been another one since.
The Choir's already on Haven, you know. Wearing someone's face. If your friend's got a new cough or a new opinion, I'd keep an eye on them.
A captain paid Mott to hide a passenger from the Hegemony, and then Mott sold the passenger's name for twice the money. He gave the captain a refund, too. The man's scrupulous.
If you ever want to know a ship's real business, buy the crew a round and ask about the third hold. Every ship on these docks has a third hold, even the ones with two.
They say the station's old reactor shielding is Concord surplus from before the war. They also say you shouldn't sleep on the Hook's lower level unless you've finished having children.

I saw that Inquisitor here, the tall one with the gloves. She bought a bowl of noodles, thanked the cook by his full legal name, and left a generous tip. He closed the stall and hasn't been seen since.
